item.title: Designing a reading surface that works at every width
item.content:encoded:
A good reading interface keeps navigation close without allowing it to compete with the article.

One information model, two compositions

Desktop screens can expose subscriptions, headlines, and the current article at once. A phone should preserve the same hierarchy as a sequence of focused views.

The layout changes, but the reader's place in the information architecture does not.

Stable controls and restrained typography make repeated reading feel calm rather than ornamental.

item.title: Local-first state and small, predictable sync files
item.description: Keep article bodies local and synchronize only subscriptions and user-authored state.

item.title: Stable identities for imperfect feeds
item.description: Prefer GUIDs, then canonical links, and use content fingerprints only as a final fallback.
